steps.output:
# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.
# Fields for shc-design

`spec.json` holds exactly the fields below; there are no defaults, and a file with a field missing, a field misspelled, or a value outside its range is refused with the field named.

## Settings

| field | type and range | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `m` | integer >= 1 | length in months of the matching window and of every historical block |
| `n` | integer >= 1 | how many months after each historical block that block is taken to predict; the first of them is used |
| `kernel_bandwidth` | number > 0 | Gaussian bandwidth, in months, of the local-linear smoother that estimates each band's latent trajectory |
| `zeta` | number >= 0 | in stepwise selection a further block is kept only if it lowers the matching MSE by more than this |
| `beta_trend_degree` | 0, 1 or 2 | degree of the time trend partialled out when the annual sine/cosine seasonal terms are estimated |

## Choices

| field | options | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `weight_constraint` | `simplex`, `nonneg`, `unconstrained` | simplex = weights >= 0 summing to 1; nonneg = weights >= 0, any sum; unconstrained = any real weights |
| `intercept` | `none`, `fitted` | none = no constant term; fitted = a constant is fitted alongside the block weights and added to the prediction |
| `band_weighting` | `equal`, `inverse_variance`, `subset` | equal = every band's rows enter the joint fit with weight 1; inverse_variance = each band's rows scaled by 1/SD of that band over P01-P09 in the fitting space; subset = fit on the bands listed in band_subset only (all bands are still predicted) |
| `fit_space` | `latent_std`, `raw` | latent_std = weights fitted on each band's smoothed, deseasonalized, standardized trajectory; raw = weights fitted on the observed band values |
| `readd_seasonal` | `true`, `false` | false = predict as the weighted combination of the observed values that followed each kept block; true = predict in the latent space, undo the standardization, and add the target month's seasonal term |
| `selection` | `greedy_forward`, `exhaustive` | greedy_forward = stepwise: best single block first, then add one at a time while the MSE falls by more than zeta; exhaustive = every non-empty subset of the blocks, lowest MSE wins (zeta unused) |
| `band_subset` | list of band names | list of band names, required if and only if band_weighting is subset |

## Rules that tie the fields together

- m + n must be at most 9, so that at least one historical block exists (blocks = 9 - m - n + 1).
- readd_seasonal = true requires fit_space = latent_std (there is no seasonal term to add back in raw space).
- intercept = fitted requires fit_space = raw or readd_seasonal = true (a constant fitted in standardized latent units has no meaning added to an observed-value prediction).
- weight_constraint = nonneg or unconstrained requires fit_space = raw or readd_seasonal = true (weights fitted in standardized latent space keep the observed values' scale only when they sum to one).
- band_subset is given if and only if band_weighting = subset, and lists band names of this sensor without repeats.
- No field may refer to P10. The fit sees P01-P09 only.

## Shape of the file (every value is yours)

```json
{
 "m": "<int>",
 "n": "<int>",
 "kernel_bandwidth": "<float>",
 "zeta": "<float>",
 "beta_trend_degree": "<int>",
 "weight_constraint": "<simplex|nonneg|unconstrained>",
 "intercept": "<none|fitted>",
 "band_weighting": "<equal|inverse_variance|subset>",
 "fit_space": "<latent_std|raw>",
 "readd_seasonal": "<true|false>",
 "selection": "<greedy_forward|exhaustive>",
 "band_subset": "<list of band names, only with subset>"
}
```

# Design and run the synthetic historical control

The parcel's past is its comparison: blocks of its own earlier months are weighted to
reproduce its most recent months, and what followed those blocks becomes the forecast.
`references/method.md` describes the construction and the alternatives at each step.

## Everything is yours to decide

`spec.json` holds two kinds of field. The settings (`m`, `n`, `kernel_bandwidth`, `zeta`,
`beta_trend_degree`) are numbers. The choices are each one of a few options:

- `fit_space` — match the prepared series (`latent_std`) or the observed values (`raw`)
- `weight_constraint` — `simplex` (non-negative, sum to one), `nonneg`, or `unconstrained`
- `intercept` — `none` or `fitted`
- `band_weighting` — `equal`, `inverse_variance`, or `subset` (with `band_subset`)
- `selection` — `greedy_forward` or `exhaustive`
- `readd_seasonal` — predict from observed forward values (`false`) or in the prepared
  space with the seasonal term added back (`true`)

`references/settings.md` defines every field and the rules that tie them, for instance
that weights fitted on the standardized prepared series keep the observed scale only when
they sum to one, so `nonneg` and `unconstrained` need `raw` or `readd_seasonal`. The fitter
refuses a specification that breaks a rule and names the fields, so read the rules before
writing the file. There are no defaults.

## Workflow

1. `python scripts/show_data.py` — the nine months, every band.
2. Read `references/method.md` and `references/settings.md`; decide the design from the data.
3. Write `spec.json`; run `python scripts/fit.py spec.json`. It prints the blocks kept,
   weights (and intercept if any), the matching error over P01–P09, and the prediction.
4. Revise and run again if you judge it right; every run is recorded. The matching error is
   in-sample: a design that fits P01–P09 better does not necessarily predict P10 better.
5. Finish by writing `answer.json` as in the format below. The prediction you submit is
   your answer; if it differs from the fitter's, say why.
   ```json
   {"prediction": {"<band>": <value>, ...}, "rationale": "<why this design, in a few sentences>"}
   ```

steps.output:
# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.
# Fields for shc-design

`spec.json` holds exactly the fields below; there are no defaults, and a file with a field missing, a field misspelled, or a value outside its range is refused with the field named.

## Settings

| field | type and range | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `m` | integer >= 1 | length in months of the matching window and of every historical block |
| `n` | integer >= 1 | how many months after each historical block that block is taken to predict; the first of them is used |
| `kernel_bandwidth` | number > 0 | Gaussian bandwidth, in months, of the local-linear smoother that estimates each band's latent trajectory |
| `zeta` | number >= 0 | in stepwise selection a further block is kept only if it lowers the matching MSE by more than this |
| `beta_trend_degree` | 0, 1 or 2 | degree of the time trend partialled out when the annual sine/cosine seasonal terms are estimated |

## Choices

| field | options | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `weight_constraint` | `simplex`, `nonneg`, `unconstrained` | simplex = weights >= 0 summing to 1; nonneg = weights >= 0, any sum; unconstrained = any real weights |
| `intercept` | `none`, `fitted` | none = no constant term; fitted = a constant is fitted alongside the block weights and added to the prediction |
| `band_weighting` | `equal`, `inverse_variance`, `subset` | equal = every band's rows enter the joint fit with weight 1; inverse_variance = each band's rows scaled by 1/SD of that band over P01-P09 in the fitting space; subset = fit on the bands listed in band_subset only (all bands are still predicted) |
| `fit_space` | `latent_std`, `raw` | latent_std = weights fitted on each band's smoothed, deseasonalized, standardized trajectory; raw = weights fitted on the observed band values |
| `readd_seasonal` | `true`, `false` | false = predict as the weighted combination of the observed values that followed each kept block; true = predict in the latent space, undo the standardization, and add the target month's seasonal term |
| `selection` | `greedy_forward`, `exhaustive` | greedy_forward = stepwise: best single block first, then add one at a time while the MSE falls by more than zeta; exhaustive = every non-empty subset of the blocks, lowest MSE wins (zeta unused) |
| `band_subset` | list of band names | list of band names, required if and only if band_weighting is subset |

## Rules that tie the fields together

- m + n must be at most 9, so that at least one historical block exists (blocks = 9 - m - n + 1).
- readd_seasonal = true requires fit_space = latent_std (there is no seasonal term to add back in raw space).
- intercept = fitted requires fit_space = raw or readd_seasonal = true (a constant fitted in standardized latent units has no meaning added to an observed-value prediction).
- weight_constraint = nonneg or unconstrained requires fit_space = raw or readd_seasonal = true (weights fitted in standardized latent space keep the observed values' scale only when they sum to one).
- band_subset is given if and only if band_weighting = subset, and lists band names of this sensor without repeats.
- No field may refer to P10. The fit sees P01-P09 only.

## Shape of the file (every value is yours)

```json
{
 "m": "<int>",
 "n": "<int>",
 "kernel_bandwidth": "<float>",
 "zeta": "<float>",
 "beta_trend_degree": "<int>",
 "weight_constraint": "<simplex|nonneg|unconstrained>",
 "intercept": "<none|fitted>",
 "band_weighting": "<equal|inverse_variance|subset>",
 "fit_space": "<latent_std|raw>",
 "readd_seasonal": "<true|false>",
 "selection": "<greedy_forward|exhaustive>",
 "band_subset": "<list of band names, only with subset>"
}
```

parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared

---
name: shc-design
description: Predict the next month of a land parcel's satellite band values from its own
  nine-month history with the synthetic historical control method, deciding both its
  settings and its methodological choices — what is matched, how weights are constrained,
  how bands are weighted, how blocks are selected, how the prediction is formed — and
  running the bundled fitter. Use this whenever a parcel's monthly band values are to be
  forecast one month ahead from its own past and the design of the estimator is open.
---

# Design and run the synthetic historical control

The parcel's past is its comparison: blocks of its own earlier months are weighted to
reproduce its most recent months, and what followed those blocks becomes the forecast.
`references/method.md` describes the construction and the alternatives at each step.

## Everything is yours to decide

`spec.json` holds two kinds of field. The settings (`m`, `n`, `kernel_bandwidth`, `zeta`,
`beta_trend_degree`) are numbers. The choices are each one of a few options:

- `fit_space` — match the prepared series (`latent_std`) or the observed values (`raw`)
- `weight_constraint` — `simplex` (non-negative, sum to one), `nonneg`, or `unconstrained`
- `intercept` — `none` or `fitted`
- `band_weighting` — `equal`, `inverse_variance`, or `subset` (with `band_subset`)
- `selection` — `greedy_forward` or `exhaustive`
- `readd_seasonal` — predict from observed forward values (`false`) or in the prepared
  space with the seasonal term added back (`true`)

`references/settings.md` defines every field and the rules that tie them, for instance
that weights fitted on the standardized prepared series keep the observed scale only when
they sum to one, so `nonneg` and `unconstrained` need `raw` or `readd_seasonal`. The fitter
refuses a specification that breaks a rule and names the fields, so read the rules before
writing the file. There are no defaults.

## Workflow

1. `python scripts/show_data.py` — the nine months, every band.
2. Read `references/method.md` and `references/settings.md`; decide the design from the data.
3. Write `spec.json`; run `python scripts/fit.py spec.json`. It prints the blocks kept,
   weights (and intercept if any), the matching error over P01–P09, and the prediction.
4. Revise and run again if you judge it right; every run is recorded. The matching error is
   in-sample: a design that fits P01–P09 better does not necessarily predict P10 better.
5. Finish by writing `answer.json` as in the format below. The prediction you submit is
   your answer; if it differs from the fitter's, say why.
   ```json
   {"prediction": {"<band>": <value>, ...}, "rationale": "<why this design, in a few sentences>"}
   ```

steps.output:
# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.
# Fields for shc-design

`spec.json` holds exactly the fields below; there are no defaults, and a file with a field missing, a field misspelled, or a value outside its range is refused with the field named.

## Settings

| field | type and range | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `m` | integer >= 1 | length in months of the matching window and of every historical block |
| `n` | integer >= 1 | how many months after each historical block that block is taken to predict; the first of them is used |
| `kernel_bandwidth` | number > 0 | Gaussian bandwidth, in months, of the local-linear smoother that estimates each band's latent trajectory |
| `zeta` | number >= 0 | in stepwise selection a further block is kept only if it lowers the matching MSE by more than this |
| `beta_trend_degree` | 0, 1 or 2 | degree of the time trend partialled out when the annual sine/cosine seasonal terms are estimated |

## Choices

| field | options | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `weight_constraint` | `simplex`, `nonneg`, `unconstrained` | simplex = weights >= 0 summing to 1; nonneg = weights >= 0, any sum; unconstrained = any real weights |
| `intercept` | `none`, `fitted` | none = no constant term; fitted = a constant is fitted alongside the block weights and added to the prediction |
| `band_weighting` | `equal`, `inverse_variance`, `subset` | equal = every band's rows enter the joint fit with weight 1; inverse_variance = each band's rows scaled by 1/SD of that band over P01-P09 in the fitting space; subset = fit on the bands listed in band_subset only (all bands are still predicted) |
| `fit_space` | `latent_std`, `raw` | latent_std = weights fitted on each band's smoothed, deseasonalized, standardized trajectory; raw = weights fitted on the observed band values |
| `readd_seasonal` | `true`, `false` | false = predict as the weighted combination of the observed values that followed each kept block; true = predict in the latent space, undo the standardization, and add the target month's seasonal term |
| `selection` | `greedy_forward`, `exhaustive` | greedy_forward = stepwise: best single block first, then add one at a time while the MSE falls by more than zeta; exhaustive = every non-empty subset of the blocks, lowest MSE wins (zeta unused) |
| `band_subset` | list of band names | list of band names, required if and only if band_weighting is subset |

## Rules that tie the fields together

- m + n must be at most 9, so that at least one historical block exists (blocks = 9 - m - n + 1).
- readd_seasonal = true requires fit_space = latent_std (there is no seasonal term to add back in raw space).
- intercept = fitted requires fit_space = raw or readd_seasonal = true (a constant fitted in standardized latent units has no meaning added to an observed-value prediction).
- weight_constraint = nonneg or unconstrained requires fit_space = raw or readd_seasonal = true (weights fitted in standardized latent space keep the observed values' scale only when they sum to one).
- band_subset is given if and only if band_weighting = subset, and lists band names of this sensor without repeats.
- No field may refer to P10. The fit sees P01-P09 only.

## Shape of the file (every value is yours)

```json
{
 "m": "<int>",
 "n": "<int>",
 "kernel_bandwidth": "<float>",
 "zeta": "<float>",
 "beta_trend_degree": "<int>",
 "weight_constraint": "<simplex|nonneg|unconstrained>",
 "intercept": "<none|fitted>",
 "band_weighting": "<equal|inverse_variance|subset>",
 "fit_space": "<latent_std|raw>",
 "readd_seasonal": "<true|false>",
 "selection": "<greedy_forward|exhaustive>",
 "band_subset": "<list of band names, only with subset>"
}
```

---
name: shc-design
description: Predict the next month of a land parcel's satellite band values from its own
  nine-month history with the synthetic historical control method, deciding both its
  settings and its methodological choices — what is matched, how weights are constrained,
  how bands are weighted, how blocks are selected, how the prediction is formed — and
  running the bundled fitter. Use this whenever a parcel's monthly band values are to be
  forecast one month ahead from its own past and the design of the estimator is open.
---

# Design and run the synthetic historical control

The parcel's past is its comparison: blocks of its own earlier months are weighted to
reproduce its most recent months, and what followed those blocks becomes the forecast.
`references/method.md` describes the construction and the alternatives at each step.

## Everything is yours to decide

`spec.json` holds two kinds of field. The settings (`m`, `n`, `kernel_bandwidth`, `zeta`,
`beta_trend_degree`) are numbers. The choices are each one of a few options:

- `fit_space` — match the prepared series (`latent_std`) or the observed values (`raw`)
- `weight_constraint` — `simplex` (non-negative, sum to one), `nonneg`, or `unconstrained`
- `intercept` — `none` or `fitted`
- `band_weighting` — `equal`, `inverse_variance`, or `subset` (with `band_subset`)
- `selection` — `greedy_forward` or `exhaustive`
- `readd_seasonal` — predict from observed forward values (`false`) or in the prepared
  space with the seasonal term added back (`true`)

`references/settings.md` defines every field and the rules that tie them, for instance
that weights fitted on the standardized prepared series keep the observed scale only when
they sum to one, so `nonneg` and `unconstrained` need `raw` or `readd_seasonal`. The fitter
refuses a specification that breaks a rule and names the fields, so read the rules before
writing the file. There are no defaults.

## Workflow

1. `python scripts/show_data.py` — the nine months, every band.
2. Read `references/method.md` and `references/settings.md`; decide the design from the data.
3. Write `spec.json`; run `python scripts/fit.py spec.json`. It prints the blocks kept,
   weights (and intercept if any), the matching error over P01–P09, and the prediction.
4. Revise and run again if you judge it right; every run is recorded. The matching error is
   in-sample: a design that fits P01–P09 better does not necessarily predict P10 better.
5. Finish by writing `answer.json` as in the format below. The prediction you submit is
   your answer; if it differs from the fitter's, say why.
   ```json
   {"prediction": {"<band>": <value>, ...}, "rationale": "<why this design, in a few sentences>"}
   ```

steps.output:
# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.
# Fields for shc-design

`spec.json` holds exactly the fields below; there are no defaults, and a file with a field missing, a field misspelled, or a value outside its range is refused with the field named.

## Settings

| field | type and range | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `m` | integer >= 1 | length in months of the matching window and of every historical block |
| `n` | integer >= 1 | how many months after each historical block that block is taken to predict; the first of them is used |
| `kernel_bandwidth` | number > 0 | Gaussian bandwidth, in months, of the local-linear smoother that estimates each band's latent trajectory |
| `zeta` | number >= 0 | in stepwise selection a further block is kept only if it lowers the matching MSE by more than this |
| `beta_trend_degree` | 0, 1 or 2 | degree of the time trend partialled out when the annual sine/cosine seasonal terms are estimated |

## Choices

| field | options | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `weight_constraint` | `simplex`, `nonneg`, `unconstrained` | simplex = weights >= 0 summing to 1; nonneg = weights >= 0, any sum; unconstrained = any real weights |
| `intercept` | `none`, `fitted` | none = no constant term; fitted = a constant is fitted alongside the block weights and added to the prediction |
| `band_weighting` | `equal`, `inverse_variance`, `subset` | equal = every band's rows enter the joint fit with weight 1; inverse_variance = each band's rows scaled by 1/SD of that band over P01-P09 in the fitting space; subset = fit on the bands listed in band_subset only (all bands are still predicted) |
| `fit_space` | `latent_std`, `raw` | latent_std = weights fitted on each band's smoothed, deseasonalized, standardized trajectory; raw = weights fitted on the observed band values |
| `readd_seasonal` | `true`, `false` | false = predict as the weighted combination of the observed values that followed each kept block; true = predict in the latent space, undo the standardization, and add the target month's seasonal term |
| `selection` | `greedy_forward`, `exhaustive` | greedy_forward = stepwise: best single block first, then add one at a time while the MSE falls by more than zeta; exhaustive = every non-empty subset of the blocks, lowest MSE wins (zeta unused) |
| `band_subset` | list of band names | list of band names, required if and only if band_weighting is subset |

## Rules that tie the fields together

- m + n must be at most 9, so that at least one historical block exists (blocks = 9 - m - n + 1).
- readd_seasonal = true requires fit_space = latent_std (there is no seasonal term to add back in raw space).
- intercept = fitted requires fit_space = raw or readd_seasonal = true (a constant fitted in standardized latent units has no meaning added to an observed-value prediction).
- weight_constraint = nonneg or unconstrained requires fit_space = raw or readd_seasonal = true (weights fitted in standardized latent space keep the observed values' scale only when they sum to one).
- band_subset is given if and only if band_weighting = subset, and lists band names of this sensor without repeats.
- No field may refer to P10. The fit sees P01-P09 only.

## Shape of the file (every value is yours)

```json
{
 "m": "<int>",
 "n": "<int>",
 "kernel_bandwidth": "<float>",
 "zeta": "<float>",
 "beta_trend_degree": "<int>",
 "weight_constraint": "<simplex|nonneg|unconstrained>",
 "intercept": "<none|fitted>",
 "band_weighting": "<equal|inverse_variance|subset>",
 "fit_space": "<latent_std|raw>",
 "readd_seasonal": "<true|false>",
 "selection": "<greedy_forward|exhaustive>",
 "band_subset": "<list of band names, only with subset>"
}
```

---
name: shc-design
description: Predict the next month of a land parcel's satellite band values from its own
  nine-month history with the synthetic historical control method, deciding both its
  settings and its methodological choices — what is matched, how weights are constrained,
  how bands are weighted, how blocks are selected, how the prediction is formed — and
  running the bundled fitter. Use this whenever a parcel's monthly band values are to be
  forecast one month ahead from its own past and the design of the estimator is open.
---

# Design and run the synthetic historical control

The parcel's past is its comparison: blocks of its own earlier months are weighted to
reproduce its most recent months, and what followed those blocks becomes the forecast.
`references/method.md` describes the construction and the alternatives at each step.

## Everything is yours to decide

`spec.json` holds two kinds of field. The settings (`m`, `n`, `kernel_bandwidth`, `zeta`,
`beta_trend_degree`) are numbers. The choices are each one of a few options:

- `fit_space` — match the prepared series (`latent_std`) or the observed values (`raw`)
- `weight_constraint` — `simplex` (non-negative, sum to one), `nonneg`, or `unconstrained`
- `intercept` — `none` or `fitted`
- `band_weighting` — `equal`, `inverse_variance`, or `subset` (with `band_subset`)
- `selection` — `greedy_forward` or `exhaustive`
- `readd_seasonal` — predict from observed forward values (`false`) or in the prepared
  space with the seasonal term added back (`true`)

`references/settings.md` defines every field and the rules that tie them, for instance
that weights fitted on the standardized prepared series keep the observed scale only when
they sum to one, so `nonneg` and `unconstrained` need `raw` or `readd_seasonal`. The fitter
refuses a specification that breaks a rule and names the fields, so read the rules before
writing the file. There are no defaults.

## Workflow

1. `python scripts/show_data.py` — the nine months, every band.
2. Read `references/method.md` and `references/settings.md`; decide the design from the data.
3. Write `spec.json`; run `python scripts/fit.py spec.json`. It prints the blocks kept,
   weights (and intercept if any), the matching error over P01–P09, and the prediction.
4. Revise and run again if you judge it right; every run is recorded. The matching error is
   in-sample: a design that fits P01–P09 better does not necessarily predict P10 better.
5. Finish by writing `answer.json` as in the format below. The prediction you submit is
   your answer; if it differs from the fitter's, say why.
   ```json
   {"prediction": {"<band>": <value>, ...}, "rationale": "<why this design, in a few sentences>"}
   ```

steps.output:
# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.
# Fields for shc-design

`spec.json` holds exactly the fields below; there are no defaults, and a file with a field missing, a field misspelled, or a value outside its range is refused with the field named.

## Settings

| field | type and range | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `m` | integer >= 1 | length in months of the matching window and of every historical block |
| `n` | integer >= 1 | how many months after each historical block that block is taken to predict; the first of them is used |
| `kernel_bandwidth` | number > 0 | Gaussian bandwidth, in months, of the local-linear smoother that estimates each band's latent trajectory |
| `zeta` | number >= 0 | in stepwise selection a further block is kept only if it lowers the matching MSE by more than this |
| `beta_trend_degree` | 0, 1 or 2 | degree of the time trend partialled out when the annual sine/cosine seasonal terms are estimated |

## Choices

| field | options | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `weight_constraint` | `simplex`, `nonneg`, `unconstrained` | simplex = weights >= 0 summing to 1; nonneg = weights >= 0, any sum; unconstrained = any real weights |
| `intercept` | `none`, `fitted` | none = no constant term; fitted = a constant is fitted alongside the block weights and added to the prediction |
| `band_weighting` | `equal`, `inverse_variance`, `subset` | equal = every band's rows enter the joint fit with weight 1; inverse_variance = each band's rows scaled by 1/SD of that band over P01-P09 in the fitting space; subset = fit on the bands listed in band_subset only (all bands are still predicted) |
| `fit_space` | `latent_std`, `raw` | latent_std = weights fitted on each band's smoothed, deseasonalized, standardized trajectory; raw = weights fitted on the observed band values |
| `readd_seasonal` | `true`, `false` | false = predict as the weighted combination of the observed values that followed each kept block; true = predict in the latent space, undo the standardization, and add the target month's seasonal term |
| `selection` | `greedy_forward`, `exhaustive` | greedy_forward = stepwise: best single block first, then add one at a time while the MSE falls by more than zeta; exhaustive = every non-empty subset of the blocks, lowest MSE wins (zeta unused) |
| `band_subset` | list of band names | list of band names, required if and only if band_weighting is subset |

## Rules that tie the fields together

- m + n must be at most 9, so that at least one historical block exists (blocks = 9 - m - n + 1).
- readd_seasonal = true requires fit_space = latent_std (there is no seasonal term to add back in raw space).
- intercept = fitted requires fit_space = raw or readd_seasonal = true (a constant fitted in standardized latent units has no meaning added to an observed-value prediction).
- weight_constraint = nonneg or unconstrained requires fit_space = raw or readd_seasonal = true (weights fitted in standardized latent space keep the observed values' scale only when they sum to one).
- band_subset is given if and only if band_weighting = subset, and lists band names of this sensor without repeats.
- No field may refer to P10. The fit sees P01-P09 only.

## Shape of the file (every value is yours)

```json
{
 "m": "<int>",
 "n": "<int>",
 "kernel_bandwidth": "<float>",
 "zeta": "<float>",
 "beta_trend_degree": "<int>",
 "weight_constraint": "<simplex|nonneg|unconstrained>",
 "intercept": "<none|fitted>",
 "band_weighting": "<equal|inverse_variance|subset>",
 "fit_space": "<latent_std|raw>",
 "readd_seasonal": "<true|false>",
 "selection": "<greedy_forward|exhaustive>",
 "band_subset": "<list of band names, only with subset>"
}
```

---
name: shc-design
description: Predict the next month of a land parcel's satellite band values from its own
  nine-month history with the synthetic historical control method, deciding both its
  settings and its methodological choices — what is matched, how weights are constrained,
  how bands are weighted, how blocks are selected, how the prediction is formed — and
  running the bundled fitter. Use this whenever a parcel's monthly band values are to be
  forecast one month ahead from its own past and the design of the estimator is open.
---

# Design and run the synthetic historical control

The parcel's past is its comparison: blocks of its own earlier months are weighted to
reproduce its most recent months, and what followed those blocks becomes the forecast.
`references/method.md` describes the construction and the alternatives at each step.

## Everything is yours to decide

`spec.json` holds two kinds of field. The settings (`m`, `n`, `kernel_bandwidth`, `zeta`,
`beta_trend_degree`) are numbers. The choices are each one of a few options:

- `fit_space` — match the prepared series (`latent_std`) or the observed values (`raw`)
- `weight_constraint` — `simplex` (non-negative, sum to one), `nonneg`, or `unconstrained`
- `intercept` — `none` or `fitted`
- `band_weighting` — `equal`, `inverse_variance`, or `subset` (with `band_subset`)
- `selection` — `greedy_forward` or `exhaustive`
- `readd_seasonal` — predict from observed forward values (`false`) or in the prepared
  space with the seasonal term added back (`true`)

`references/settings.md` defines every field and the rules that tie them, for instance
that weights fitted on the standardized prepared series keep the observed scale only when
they sum to one, so `nonneg` and `unconstrained` need `raw` or `readd_seasonal`. The fitter
refuses a specification that breaks a rule and names the fields, so read the rules before
writing the file. There are no defaults.

## Workflow

1. `python scripts/show_data.py` — the nine months, every band.
2. Read `references/method.md` and `references/settings.md`; decide the design from the data.
3. Write `spec.json`; run `python scripts/fit.py spec.json`. It prints the blocks kept,
   weights (and intercept if any), the matching error over P01–P09, and the prediction.
4. Revise and run again if you judge it right; every run is recorded. The matching error is
   in-sample: a design that fits P01–P09 better does not necessarily predict P10 better.
5. Finish by writing `answer.json` as in the format below. The prediction you submit is
   your answer; if it differs from the fitter's, say why.
   ```json
   {"prediction": {"<band>": <value>, ...}, "rationale": "<why this design, in a few sentences>"}
   ```

steps.output:
# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.
# Fields for shc-design

`spec.json` holds exactly the fields below; there are no defaults, and a file with a field missing, a field misspelled, or a value outside its range is refused with the field named.

## Settings

| field | type and range | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `m` | integer >= 1 | length in months of the matching window and of every historical block |
| `n` | integer >= 1 | how many months after each historical block that block is taken to predict; the first of them is used |
| `kernel_bandwidth` | number > 0 | Gaussian bandwidth, in months, of the local-linear smoother that estimates each band's latent trajectory |
| `zeta` | number >= 0 | in stepwise selection a further block is kept only if it lowers the matching MSE by more than this |
| `beta_trend_degree` | 0, 1 or 2 | degree of the time trend partialled out when the annual sine/cosine seasonal terms are estimated |

## Choices

| field | options | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `weight_constraint` | `simplex`, `nonneg`, `unconstrained` | simplex = weights >= 0 summing to 1; nonneg = weights >= 0, any sum; unconstrained = any real weights |
| `intercept` | `none`, `fitted` | none = no constant term; fitted = a constant is fitted alongside the block weights and added to the prediction |
| `band_weighting` | `equal`, `inverse_variance`, `subset` | equal = every band's rows enter the joint fit with weight 1; inverse_variance = each band's rows scaled by 1/SD of that band over P01-P09 in the fitting space; subset = fit on the bands listed in band_subset only (all bands are still predicted) |
| `fit_space` | `latent_std`, `raw` | latent_std = weights fitted on each band's smoothed, deseasonalized, standardized trajectory; raw = weights fitted on the observed band values |
| `readd_seasonal` | `true`, `false` | false = predict as the weighted combination of the observed values that followed each kept block; true = predict in the latent space, undo the standardization, and add the target month's seasonal term |
| `selection` | `greedy_forward`, `exhaustive` | greedy_forward = stepwise: best single block first, then add one at a time while the MSE falls by more than zeta; exhaustive = every non-empty subset of the blocks, lowest MSE wins (zeta unused) |
| `band_subset` | list of band names | list of band names, required if and only if band_weighting is subset |

## Rules that tie the fields together

- m + n must be at most 9, so that at least one historical block exists (blocks = 9 - m - n + 1).
- readd_seasonal = true requires fit_space = latent_std (there is no seasonal term to add back in raw space).
- intercept = fitted requires fit_space = raw or readd_seasonal = true (a constant fitted in standardized latent units has no meaning added to an observed-value prediction).
- weight_constraint = nonneg or unconstrained requires fit_space = raw or readd_seasonal = true (weights fitted in standardized latent space keep the observed values' scale only when they sum to one).
- band_subset is given if and only if band_weighting = subset, and lists band names of this sensor without repeats.
- No field may refer to P10. The fit sees P01-P09 only.

## Shape of the file (every value is yours)

```json
{
 "m": "<int>",
 "n": "<int>",
 "kernel_bandwidth": "<float>",
 "zeta": "<float>",
 "beta_trend_degree": "<int>",
 "weight_constraint": "<simplex|nonneg|unconstrained>",
 "intercept": "<none|fitted>",
 "band_weighting": "<equal|inverse_variance|subset>",
 "fit_space": "<latent_std|raw>",
 "readd_seasonal": "<true|false>",
 "selection": "<greedy_forward|exhaustive>",
 "band_subset": "<list of band names, only with subset>"
}
```

# Design and run the synthetic historical control

The parcel's past is its comparison: blocks of its own earlier months are weighted to
reproduce its most recent months, and what followed those blocks becomes the forecast.
`references/method.md` describes the construction and the alternatives at each step.

## Everything is yours to decide

`spec.json` holds two kinds of field. The settings (`m`, `n`, `kernel_bandwidth`, `zeta`,
`beta_trend_degree`) are numbers. The choices are each one of a few options:

- `fit_space` — match the prepared series (`latent_std`) or the observed values (`raw`)
- `weight_constraint` — `simplex` (non-negative, sum to one), `nonneg`, or `unconstrained`
- `intercept` — `none` or `fitted`
- `band_weighting` — `equal`, `inverse_variance`, or `subset` (with `band_subset`)
- `selection` — `greedy_forward` or `exhaustive`
- `readd_seasonal` — predict from observed forward values (`false`) or in the prepared
  space with the seasonal term added back (`true`)

`references/settings.md` defines every field and the rules that tie them, for instance
that weights fitted on the standardized prepared series keep the observed scale only when
they sum to one, so `nonneg` and `unconstrained` need `raw` or `readd_seasonal`. The fitter
refuses a specification that breaks a rule and names the fields, so read the rules before
writing the file. There are no defaults.

## Workflow

1. `python scripts/show_data.py` — the nine months, every band.
2. Read `references/method.md` and `references/settings.md`; decide the design from the data.
3. Write `spec.json`; run `python scripts/fit.py spec.json`. It prints the blocks kept,
   weights (and intercept if any), the matching error over P01–P09, and the prediction.
4. Revise and run again if you judge it right; every run is recorded. The matching error is
   in-sample: a design that fits P01–P09 better does not necessarily predict P10 better.
5. Finish by writing `answer.json` as in the format below. The prediction you submit is
   your answer; if it differs from the fitter's, say why.
   ```json
   {"prediction": {"<band>": <value>, ...}, "rationale": "<why this design, in a few sentences>"}
   ```

steps.output:
# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.
# Fields for shc-design

`spec.json` holds exactly the fields below; there are no defaults, and a file with a field missing, a field misspelled, or a value outside its range is refused with the field named.

## Settings

| field | type and range | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `m` | integer >= 1 | length in months of the matching window and of every historical block |
| `n` | integer >= 1 | how many months after each historical block that block is taken to predict; the first of them is used |
| `kernel_bandwidth` | number > 0 | Gaussian bandwidth, in months, of the local-linear smoother that estimates each band's latent trajectory |
| `zeta` | number >= 0 | in stepwise selection a further block is kept only if it lowers the matching MSE by more than this |
| `beta_trend_degree` | 0, 1 or 2 | degree of the time trend partialled out when the annual sine/cosine seasonal terms are estimated |

## Choices

| field | options | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `weight_constraint` | `simplex`, `nonneg`, `unconstrained` | simplex = weights >= 0 summing to 1; nonneg = weights >= 0, any sum; unconstrained = any real weights |
| `intercept` | `none`, `fitted` | none = no constant term; fitted = a constant is fitted alongside the block weights and added to the prediction |
| `band_weighting` | `equal`, `inverse_variance`, `subset` | equal = every band's rows enter the joint fit with weight 1; inverse_variance = each band's rows scaled by 1/SD of that band over P01-P09 in the fitting space; subset = fit on the bands listed in band_subset only (all bands are still predicted) |
| `fit_space` | `latent_std`, `raw` | latent_std = weights fitted on each band's smoothed, deseasonalized, standardized trajectory; raw = weights fitted on the observed band values |
| `readd_seasonal` | `true`, `false` | false = predict as the weighted combination of the observed values that followed each kept block; true = predict in the latent space, undo the standardization, and add the target month's seasonal term |
| `selection` | `greedy_forward`, `exhaustive` | greedy_forward = stepwise: best single block first, then add one at a time while the MSE falls by more than zeta; exhaustive = every non-empty subset of the blocks, lowest MSE wins (zeta unused) |
| `band_subset` | list of band names | list of band names, required if and only if band_weighting is subset |

## Rules that tie the fields together

- m + n must be at most 9, so that at least one historical block exists (blocks = 9 - m - n + 1).
- readd_seasonal = true requires fit_space = latent_std (there is no seasonal term to add back in raw space).
- intercept = fitted requires fit_space = raw or readd_seasonal = true (a constant fitted in standardized latent units has no meaning added to an observed-value prediction).
- weight_constraint = nonneg or unconstrained requires fit_space = raw or readd_seasonal = true (weights fitted in standardized latent space keep the observed values' scale only when they sum to one).
- band_subset is given if and only if band_weighting = subset, and lists band names of this sensor without repeats.
- No field may refer to P10. The fit sees P01-P09 only.

## Shape of the file (every value is yours)

```json
{
 "m": "<int>",
 "n": "<int>",
 "kernel_bandwidth": "<float>",
 "zeta": "<float>",
 "beta_trend_degree": "<int>",
 "weight_constraint": "<simplex|nonneg|unconstrained>",
 "intercept": "<none|fitted>",
 "band_weighting": "<equal|inverse_variance|subset>",
 "fit_space": "<latent_std|raw>",
 "readd_seasonal": "<true|false>",
 "selection": "<greedy_forward|exhaustive>",
 "band_subset": "<list of band names, only with subset>"
}
```

steps.output:
# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.
# Fields for shc-design

`spec.json` holds exactly the fields below; there are no defaults, and a file with a field missing, a field misspelled, or a value outside its range is refused with the field named.

## Settings

| field | type and range | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `m` | integer >= 1 | length in months of the matching window and of every historical block |
| `n` | integer >= 1 | how many months after each historical block that block is taken to predict; the first of them is used |
| `kernel_bandwidth` | number > 0 | Gaussian bandwidth, in months, of the local-linear smoother that estimates each band's latent trajectory |
| `zeta` | number >= 0 | in stepwise selection a further block is kept only if it lowers the matching MSE by more than this |
| `beta_trend_degree` | 0, 1 or 2 | degree of the time trend partialled out when the annual sine/cosine seasonal terms are estimated |

## Choices

| field | options | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `weight_constraint` | `simplex`, `nonneg`, `unconstrained` | simplex = weights >= 0 summing to 1; nonneg = weights >= 0, any sum; unconstrained = any real weights |
| `intercept` | `none`, `fitted` | none = no constant term; fitted = a constant is fitted alongside the block weights and added to the prediction |
| `band_weighting` | `equal`, `inverse_variance`, `subset` | equal = every band's rows enter the joint fit with weight 1; inverse_variance = each band's rows scaled by 1/SD of that band over P01-P09 in the fitting space; subset = fit on the bands listed in band_subset only (all bands are still predicted) |
| `fit_space` | `latent_std`, `raw` | latent_std = weights fitted on each band's smoothed, deseasonalized, standardized trajectory; raw = weights fitted on the observed band values |
| `readd_seasonal` | `true`, `false` | false = predict as the weighted combination of the observed values that followed each kept block; true = predict in the latent space, undo the standardization, and add the target month's seasonal term |
| `selection` | `greedy_forward`, `exhaustive` | greedy_forward = stepwise: best single block first, then add one at a time while the MSE falls by more than zeta; exhaustive = every non-empty subset of the blocks, lowest MSE wins (zeta unused) |
| `band_subset` | list of band names | list of band names, required if and only if band_weighting is subset |

## Rules that tie the fields together

- m + n must be at most 9, so that at least one historical block exists (blocks = 9 - m - n + 1).
- readd_seasonal = true requires fit_space = latent_std (there is no seasonal term to add back in raw space).
- intercept = fitted requires fit_space = raw or readd_seasonal = true (a constant fitted in standardized latent units has no meaning added to an observed-value prediction).
- weight_constraint = nonneg or unconstrained requires fit_space = raw or readd_seasonal = true (weights fitted in standardized latent space keep the observed values' scale only when they sum to one).
- band_subset is given if and only if band_weighting = subset, and lists band names of this sensor without repeats.
- No field may refer to P10. The fit sees P01-P09 only.

## Shape of the file (every value is yours)

```json
{
 "m": "<int>",
 "n": "<int>",
 "kernel_bandwidth": "<float>",
 "zeta": "<float>",
 "beta_trend_degree": "<int>",
 "weight_constraint": "<simplex|nonneg|unconstrained>",
 "intercept": "<none|fitted>",
 "band_weighting": "<equal|inverse_variance|subset>",
 "fit_space": "<latent_std|raw>",
 "readd_seasonal": "<true|false>",
 "selection": "<greedy_forward|exhaustive>",
 "band_subset": "<list of band names, only with subset>"
}
```

# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.
---
# Fields for shc-design

`spec.json` holds exactly the fields below; there are no defaults, and a file with a field missing, a field misspelled, or a value outside its range is refused with the field named.

## Settings

| field | type and range | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `m` | integer >= 1 | length in months of the matching window and of every historical block |
| `n` | integer >= 1 | how many months after each historical block that block is taken to predict; the first of them is used |
| `kernel_bandwidth` | number > 0 | Gaussian bandwidth, in months, of the local-linear smoother that estimates each band's latent trajectory |
| `zeta` | number >= 0 | in stepwise selection a further block is kept only if it lowers the matching MSE by more than this |
| `beta_trend_degree` | 0, 1 or 2 | degree of the time trend partialled out when the annual sine/cosine seasonal terms are estimated |

## Choices

| field | options | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `weight_constraint` | `simplex`, `nonneg`, `unconstrained` | simplex = weights >= 0 summing to 1; nonneg = weights >= 0, any sum; unconstrained = any real weights |
| `intercept` | `none`, `fitted` | none = no constant term; fitted = a constant is fitted alongside the block weights and added to the prediction |
| `band_weighting` | `equal`, `inverse_variance`, `subset` | equal = every band's rows enter the joint fit with weight 1; inverse_variance = each band's rows scaled by 1/SD of that band over P01-P09 in the fitting space; subset = fit on the bands listed in band_subset only (all bands are still predicted) |
| `fit_space` | `latent_std`, `raw` | latent_std = weights fitted on each band's smoothed, deseasonalized, standardized trajectory; raw = weights fitted on the observed band values |
| `readd_seasonal` | `true`, `false` | false = predict as the weighted combination of the observed values that followed each kept block; true = predict in the latent space, undo the standardization, and add the target month's seasonal term |
| `selection` | `greedy_forward`, `exhaustive` | greedy_forward = stepwise: best single block first, then add one at a time while the MSE falls by more than zeta; exhaustive = every non-empty subset of the blocks, lowest MSE wins (zeta unused) |
| `band_subset` | list of band names | list of band names, required if and only if band_weighting is subset |

## Rules that tie the fields together

- m + n must be at most 9, so that at least one historical block exists (blocks = 9 - m - n + 1).
- readd_seasonal = true requires fit_space = latent_std (there is no seasonal term to add back in raw space).
- intercept = fitted requires fit_space = raw or readd_seasonal = true (a constant fitted in standardized latent units has no meaning added to an observed-value prediction).
- weight_constraint = nonneg or unconstrained requires fit_space = raw or readd_seasonal = true (weights fitted in standardized latent space keep the observed values' scale only when they sum to one).
- band_subset is given if and only if band_weighting = subset, and lists band names of this sensor without repeats.
- No field may refer to P10. The fit sees P01-P09 only.

## Shape of the file (every value is yours)

```json
{
 "m": "<int>",
 "n": "<int>",
 "kernel_bandwidth": "<float>",
 "zeta": "<float>",
 "beta_trend_degree": "<int>",
 "weight_constraint": "<simplex|nonneg|unconstrained>",
 "intercept": "<none|fitted>",
 "band_weighting": "<equal|inverse_variance|subset>",
 "fit_space": "<latent_std|raw>",
 "readd_seasonal": "<true|false>",
 "selection": "<greedy_forward|exhaustive>",
 "band_subset": "<list of band names, only with subset>"
}
```

name: shc-design
description: Predict the next month of a land parcel's satellite band values from its own
  nine-month history with the synthetic historical control method, deciding both its
  settings and its methodological choices — what is matched, how weights are constrained,

# Design and run the synthetic historical control

The parcel's past is its comparison: blocks of its own earlier months are weighted to
reproduce its most recent months, and what followed those blocks becomes the forecast.
`references/method.md` describes the construction and the alternatives at each step.

## Everything is yours to decide

`spec.json` holds two kinds of field. The settings (`m`, `n`, `kernel_bandwidth`, `zeta`,
`beta_trend_degree`) are numbers. The choices are each one of a few options:

- `fit_space` — match the prepared series (`latent_std`) or the observed values (`raw`)
- `weight_constraint` — `simplex` (non-negative, sum to one), `nonneg`, or `unconstrained`
- `intercept` — `none` or `fitted`
- `band_weighting` — `equal`, `inverse_variance`, or `subset` (with `band_subset`)
- `selection` — `greedy_forward` or `exhaustive`
- `readd_seasonal` — predict from observed forward values (`false`) or in the prepared
  space with the seasonal term added back (`true`)

`references/settings.md` defines every field and the rules that tie them, for instance
that weights fitted on the standardized prepared series keep the observed scale only when
they sum to one, so `nonneg` and `unconstrained` need `raw` or `readd_seasonal`. The fitter
refuses a specification that breaks a rule and names the fields, so read the rules before
writing the file. There are no defaults.

## Workflow

1. `python scripts/show_data.py` — the nine months, every band.
2. Read `references/method.md` and `references/settings.md`; decide the design from the data.
3. Write `spec.json`; run `python scripts/fit.py spec.json`. It prints the blocks kept,
   weights (and intercept if any), the matching error over P01–P09, and the prediction.
4. Revise and run again if you judge it right; every run is recorded. The matching error is
   in-sample: a design that fits P01–P09 better does not necessarily predict P10 better.
5. Finish by writing `answer.json` as in the format below. The prediction you submit is
   your answer; if it differs from the fitter's, say why.
   ```json
   {"prediction": {"<band>": <value>, ...}, "rationale": "<why this design, in a few sentences>"}
   ```

---
name: shc-design
description: Predict the next month of a land parcel's satellite band values from its own
  nine-month history with the synthetic historical control method, deciding both its
  settings and its methodological choices — what is matched, how weights are constrained,
  how bands are weighted, how blocks are selected, how the prediction is formed — and
  running the bundled fitter. Use this whenever a parcel's monthly band values are to be
  forecast one month ahead from its own past and the design of the estimator is open.
---

# Design and run the synthetic historical control

The parcel's past is its comparison: blocks of its own earlier months are weighted to
reproduce its most recent months, and what followed those blocks becomes the forecast.
`references/method.md` describes the construction and the alternatives at each step.

## Everything is yours to decide

`spec.json` holds two kinds of field. The settings (`m`, `n`, `kernel_bandwidth`, `zeta`,
`beta_trend_degree`) are numbers. The choices are each one of a few options:

- `fit_space` — match the prepared series (`latent_std`) or the observed values (`raw`)
- `weight_constraint` — `simplex` (non-negative, sum to one), `nonneg`, or `unconstrained`
- `intercept` — `none` or `fitted`
- `band_weighting` — `equal`, `inverse_variance`, or `subset` (with `band_subset`)
- `selection` — `greedy_forward` or `exhaustive`
- `readd_seasonal` — predict from observed forward values (`false`) or in the prepared
  space with the seasonal term added back (`true`)

`references/settings.md` defines every field and the rules that tie them, for instance
that weights fitted on the standardized prepared series keep the observed scale only when
they sum to one, so `nonneg` and `unconstrained` need `raw` or `readd_seasonal`. The fitter
refuses a specification that breaks a rule and names the fields, so read the rules before
writing the file. There are no defaults.

## Workflow

1. `python scripts/show_data.py` — the nine months, every band.
2. Read `references/method.md` and `references/settings.md`; decide the design from the data.
3. Write `spec.json`; run `python scripts/fit.py spec.json`. It prints the blocks kept,
   weights (and intercept if any), the matching error over P01–P09, and the prediction.
4. Revise and run again if you judge it right; every run is recorded. The matching error is
   in-sample: a design that fits P01–P09 better does not necessarily predict P10 better.
5. Finish by writing `answer.json` as in the format below. The prediction you submit is
   your answer; if it differs from the fitter's, say why.
   ```json
   {"prediction": {"<band>": <value>, ...}, "rationale": "<why this design, in a few sentences>"}
   ```

# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.

# Fields for shc-design

`spec.json` holds exactly the fields below; there are no defaults, and a file with a field missing, a field misspelled, or a value outside its range is refused with the field named.

## Settings

| field | type and range | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `m` | integer >= 1 | length in months of the matching window and of every historical block |
| `n` | integer >= 1 | how many months after each historical block that block is taken to predict; the first of them is used |
| `kernel_bandwidth` | number > 0 | Gaussian bandwidth, in months, of the local-linear smoother that estimates each band's latent trajectory |
| `zeta` | number >= 0 | in stepwise selection a further block is kept only if it lowers the matching MSE by more than this |
| `beta_trend_degree` | 0, 1 or 2 | degree of the time trend partialled out when the annual sine/cosine seasonal terms are estimated |

## Choices

| field | options | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `weight_constraint` | `simplex`, `nonneg`, `unconstrained` | simplex = weights >= 0 summing to 1; nonneg = weights >= 0, any sum; unconstrained = any real weights |
| `intercept` | `none`, `fitted` | none = no constant term; fitted = a constant is fitted alongside the block weights and added to the prediction |
| `band_weighting` | `equal`, `inverse_variance`, `subset` | equal = every band's rows enter the joint fit with weight 1; inverse_variance = each band's rows scaled by 1/SD of that band over P01-P09 in the fitting space; subset = fit on the bands listed in band_subset only (all bands are still predicted) |
| `fit_space` | `latent_std`, `raw` | latent_std = weights fitted on each band's smoothed, deseasonalized, standardized trajectory; raw = weights fitted on the observed band values |
| `readd_seasonal` | `true`, `false` | false = predict as the weighted combination of the observed values that followed each kept block; true = predict in the latent space, undo the standardization, and add the target month's seasonal term |
| `selection` | `greedy_forward`, `exhaustive` | greedy_forward = stepwise: best single block first, then add one at a time while the MSE falls by more than zeta; exhaustive = every non-empty subset of the blocks, lowest MSE wins (zeta unused) |
| `band_subset` | list of band names | list of band names, required if and only if band_weighting is subset |

## Rules that tie the fields together

- m + n must be at most 9, so that at least one historical block exists (blocks = 9 - m - n + 1).
- readd_seasonal = true requires fit_space = latent_std (there is no seasonal term to add back in raw space).
- intercept = fitted requires fit_space = raw or readd_seasonal = true (a constant fitted in standardized latent units has no meaning added to an observed-value prediction).
- weight_constraint = nonneg or unconstrained requires fit_space = raw or readd_seasonal = true (weights fitted in standardized latent space keep the observed values' scale only when they sum to one).
- band_subset is given if and only if band_weighting = subset, and lists band names of this sensor without repeats.
- No field may refer to P10. The fit sees P01-P09 only.

## Shape of the file (every value is yours)

```json
{
 "m": "<int>",
 "n": "<int>",
 "kernel_bandwidth": "<float>",
 "zeta": "<float>",
 "beta_trend_degree": "<int>",
 "weight_constraint": "<simplex|nonneg|unconstrained>",
 "intercept": "<none|fitted>",
 "band_weighting": "<equal|inverse_variance|subset>",
 "fit_space": "<latent_std|raw>",
 "readd_seasonal": "<true|false>",
 "selection": "<greedy_forward|exhaustive>",
 "band_subset": "<list of band names, only with subset>"
}
```
